CHM-01
It is 5.45 am, fog is sitting in the hollows, chimney smoke is hanging flat and the wind meter reads 1 km/h. The label says 3 to 20 km/h. What do you do?
Spray anyway - greens are always done at dawn
Raise the boom so the job is finished sooner
Hold off, tell your supervisor, recheck later
Spray the greens nearest the boundary first
C
Calm, foggy conditions with smoke hanging flat signal a surface temperature inversion, and the wind is below the label minimum. Wait and recheck.
CHM-01
Which part of the spray job carries the biggest exposure risk?
Mixing and loading the concentrate
Driving the sprayer back to the shed
Reading the spray sheet in the office
Walking the area after re-entry time
A
Concentrate is the strongest form of the product, so splashes while measuring and pouring matter most. Full label PPE every mix and fill.
CHM-01
Where should the fill hose be while the spray tank fills?
Pushed to the bottom of the tank to stop splashing
Above the opening with an air gap, not in the mix
Tied inside the tank so it cannot fall out
Anywhere, as long as a backflow device is on site
B
A hose below the water can siphon tank mix back into the water supply if pressure drops. Keep an air gap and use the fill point backflow device.
CHM-01
The label gives no mixing order. After water and any water conditioner, what goes in next?
Wetters and surfactants (adjuvants)
Soluble liquid concentrates (SL)
Emulsifiable concentrates (EC)
Water-dispersible granules (WG)
D
General order: water conditioners, dry products such as WG and wettable powders, ECs and oils, soluble liquids, then wetters. The label order always wins.
CHM-01
You have just emptied a 10 L fungicide container into the induction hopper. What now?
Cap it and put it in the skip with the rubbish
Triple rinse now; add the rinsings to the tank
Store it and rinse a batch at month end
Rinse it once at the wash bay, down the drain
B
Rinse immediately while residue is wet, add the rinsings to the spray tank, then drain, remove the lid and store it for drumMUSTER or CHM-03 disposal.
CHM-01
Disease pressure is high and a co-worker suggests going 50 percent over the label rate. What is the right response?
Agree, as long as it goes on the spray record
Agree, but only for the greens this time
No - above-label rates need a permit
Split the difference and go 25 percent over
C
In Victoria, using more than the label rate needs a permit. Product, rate and mix decisions belong to the Course Superintendent - follow the spray sheet.
CHM-01
You are spraying a fairway when a golfer walks onto the area ahead of you. What do you do?
Stop spraying and wait until they are clear
Keep going - they can see the warning sign
Wave them through, then spray in behind them
Turn the pressure down and keep spraying
A
Never spray near people. Stop, wait until they are clear, and keep people off until the re-entry period has passed (CHM-04).
CHM-01
You have finished spraying and it is smoko. What is the right order?
Eat in the sprayer cab, then wash up after
Take your overalls into the lunchroom with you
Wash your hands only if they look dirty
PPE off in the spray area, wash, then eat
D
Wash gloves, take PPE off in the spray area, wash hands, arms and face, then eat in the lunchroom. Contaminated PPE never goes into lunchrooms, cabs or home.
CHM-01
Under Victorian law, how soon must the chemical use record be made, and how long is it kept?
Within 48 hours; kept for 2 years
Within 7 days; kept for 1 year
By month end; kept for 6 months
Within 24 hours; kept for 5 years
A
Records are required within 48 hours of use and kept for 2 years. Our standard is to complete and sign the spray record the same day.
CHM-01
There is 40 L of mix left in the tank at the end of the job. What do you do with it?
Tip it down the wash bay drain and rinse
Apply as the label and supervisor direct
Keep it in the tank for tomorrow's job
Empty it on the gravel behind the shed
B
Leftover mix usually goes over the treated area at or below the label rate, as directed. Never into drains, onto hard surfaces or near water.
CHM-05
Concentrate splashes into your eye while you are pouring at the mixing bay. What do you do?
Finish pouring, then rinse the eye well at smoko
Blink hard, wipe it with a clean rag and carry on
Flush at the eyewash 15+ minutes, eyelids open
Use normal eye drops, then see how it feels later
C
Water is the first treatment and time matters. Flush at least 15 minutes (longer for corrosives), then call 13 11 26 or get medical help.
CHM-05
Tank mix has soaked through your sleeve onto your arm. What is the first aid?
Clothing off, flood with water, then soap and water
Let it dry on the skin, then brush off any residue
Wipe it off with a rag dampened with clean diesel
Roll the sleeve up and rinse it at the end of the job
A
Get the source off the skin first, then water and soap. Never use fuel or solvent on skin. Bag the clothing and report it.
CHM-05
A co-worker has swallowed some spray mix from a mislabelled bottle. What should you do?
Make them vomit straight away to get it out
Give them a glass of milk to neutralise it
Wait an hour to see if any symptoms develop
Rinse mouth, no vomiting, call 13 11 26
D
ANZCOR advises rinsing the mouth and not inducing vomiting or giving anything to neutralise. Get expert advice straight away - 000 if they are unwell.
CHM-05
You find a co-worker dizzy on the floor of the chemical store next to a leaking container, with a strong smell. What do you do?
Run in and carry them out before anything else
Call for help and 000; go in only if it is safe
Shut the store door to keep the fumes contained
Clean up the leaking container first so it stops
B
Protect yourself first. Call for help and 000, ventilate from outside if you can, and move them to fresh air only when it is safe.
CHM-05
Which of these needs a 000 call straight away?
A small splash on a glove, washed off at once
A drip on the wrist, washed off, worker feels fine
Struggling to breathe after being caught in drift
A worker whose goggles have a scratched lens
C
Difficulty breathing, being unresponsive or very drowsy, a seizure, any chemical burn to the skin or eyes, or getting worse - call 000.
CHM-05
Someone is going to hospital after a chemical exposure. What should go with them?
The SDS or a clear photo of the product label
The contaminated container, on the back seat
Nothing - the hospital will work it out itself
The spray sheet for the next scheduled job
A
Doctors need the product identity. Send the SDS or label details, but do not put a contaminated container in the vehicle.
CHM-05
You finished spraying for the day and your work clothes have spray on them. What should happen to them?
Wash them at home with the family washing
Hang them up in the lunchroom to dry out
Wear them home and wash them at the weekend
Keep them in the spray area; wash separately
D
Contaminated clothing stays out of lunchrooms, cars and homes, and is washed separately. Soaked clothing is bagged for your supervisor to decide on.
CHM-05
A crew member had a small splash on their wrist, washed it off straight away and feels fine. Should it be reported?
No - it was washed off and nothing happened
Yes - supervisor, #ohs and the form
Only if a rash appears within the next week
Only if another crew member saw it happen
B
Every exposure is reported so the cause can be fixed - a torn glove, a leaking fitting or a missing face shield.
CHM-05
A worker needs medical treatment the day after a chemical exposure at work. What must management do?
Nothing, provided the worker is back at work
Phone WorkSafe now, then notify in writing
Raise it at the next monthly toolbox talk
Note it on the spray record for that day
B
Medical treatment within 48 hours of exposure to a substance is notifiable: phone WorkSafe immediately on 13 23 60, then written notice within 48 hours (OHS-13).
CHM-05
Under Victoria's OHS Regulations, when is health monitoring required for a pesticide?
Whenever anyone on the crew sprays any pesticide at all
Only when a worker asks the Club to arrange a blood test
When exposure to a listed substance is likely to harm health
Never - health monitoring only applies in factories and labs
C
Schedule 9 lists organophosphate pesticides. Monitoring is supervised by a doctor, arranged by the employer, and does not replace PPE.
OHS-01
It is your second day and the crew is short. A crew member offers to show you the controls of a ride-on you are not signed off on so you can mow the tees. What do you do?
Mow the tees slowly now you know the controls
Read the SWP on your phone, then mow the tees
Say you are not signed off and tell your supervisor
Mow only the flat tees and keep well clear of the banks
C
Being shown the controls is not a sign-off. You need training, sign-off and a signed SWP before you operate any machine.
OHS-01
You are raking a bunker when a golf ball lands a metre from you. Nobody is hurt. What should you do?
Move clear, then post in #ohs and fill in the form
Carry on - a near miss with nobody hurt is not reported
Mention it to a mate at smoko so they stay alert
Raise it at the next toolbox talk if you remember
A
It is a near miss. Every hazard, near miss and incident is reported in #ohs and on the form - near misses show where the next injury could come from.
OHS-01
You are mowing the 12th. Where do lightning and severe-weather alerts arrive?
Slack #ohs, with hazard reports
TurfDog, at the top of the job list
A text message from your supervisor
Slack #course-team, from UBIMET
D
UBIMET lightning and severe-weather alerts arrive in #course-team. Act on them straight away and follow OHS-04.
OHS-01
You were out late at a party and are rostered for a 5am start. Which is correct?
The rule is 0.00 - tell your supervisor before you start
You are fine to start as long as you are under 0.05
It only matters if you drive on a public road later that day
Coffee and a cold shower will clear it before 5am
A
The Club rule is zero alcohol while working, driving or operating machinery. Alcohol can still be in your system next morning, and coffee or a cold shower will not clear it.
OHS-01
During your pre-start check you find a leaking hydraulic hose on a mower. What do you do?
Use it gently and report it at the end of the day
Swap to another mower and keep it to yourself
Fix the hose yourself so the job is not held up
Tag it out of service and tell your supervisor
D
Faulty equipment is tagged out and reported so nobody else uses it. Never use a machine that is tagged out (OHS-14).
OHS-01
Which of these is one of your legal duties as an employee under the Victorian OHS Act?
Take reasonable care for yourself and others
Supply your own PPE and safety equipment
Investigate every incident you are involved in
Notify WorkSafe yourself of any injury
A
Employees must take reasonable care for themselves and others, cooperate with safety measures, and not misuse or interfere with safety equipment.
OHS-01
You think a job you have been given is unsafe. What should you do?
Do it anyway - speaking up could cost you your shifts
Stop and tell your supervisor - you are protected
Do it, then complain about it on social media
Leave site quietly without saying anything
B
Raise safety concerns with your supervisor, then the Course Superintendent or management if needed. An employer must not punish you for raising a health and safety issue.
OHS-01
You are mowing an approach and a golfer is standing on the tee. What should you do?
Keep going - golfers have to wait for maintenance
Speed up so you are out of the way sooner
Stop, wait and make sure they have seen you
Give them a wave and keep mowing steadily
C
Never assume a golfer has seen you. Stop and wait when someone is about to hit, and make sure they have seen you before you move (OHS-16).
OHS-01
Your phone rings while you are operating a ride-on mower. What do you do?
Answer it - it could be your supervisor
Stop somewhere safe before you answer
Answer on speaker and keep mowing slowly
Put it in the basket so it cannot distract you
B
Never use your phone while operating a machine or driving. Stop somewhere safe first - and keep your phone on you, not in the machine.
OHS-01
You would like the crew to have a health and safety representative (HSR). What can you do?
Nothing - only management can decide that
Appoint yourself HSR and tell the crew
Lodge a request with the Fair Work Commission
Ask for a designated work group to be set up
D
Employees can be represented by an elected HSR. Asking for a designated work group is the first step - the employer must do everything reasonable to start negotiations within 14 days.
OHS-02
You find a crew member collapsed on the 14th green. Which radio call is right?
"Can someone come down to 14 when you get a chance? Something seems to be up with Jack."
"Base, base, is anyone there? I need someone to call me back on my mobile now."
"Emergency, emergency, emergency. Sam, 14th green. Jack down, not breathing, need AED."
"Something has happened on 14. I will call back in a minute or so once I know a bit more."
C
Say "Emergency" three times, then who, where, what you need and whether 000 has been called. Vague calls waste time.
OHS-02
You are mowing the 3rd when you hear "Emergency, emergency, emergency" on the radio. What should you do?
Stay off the radio unless you are closest or have the AED
Call in straight away and ask what has happened and where
Turn the radio down so the chatter does not distract you
Drive over to the area to see whether you can help out
A
The channel must stay clear for the emergency. Only speak if it helps - for example you are closest or have the AED.
OHS-02
You are through to the 000 call-taker about a fire in the workshop. What do they need first?
Your full name, date of birth and home address
The name and mobile number of your supervisor
A description of what the workshop is used for
Location - the address, the spot and the gate
D
Location is the most important thing. A golf course is hard to find, so give the address, the exact spot and the gate.
OHS-02
Why should you have the Emergency+ app on your phone?
It sends your current job details straight to TurfDog
It shows your GPS position and a what3words address
It lets you turn off the gas and power from your phone
It sends an alert, so you no longer need to call 000
B
Emergency+ shows GPS coordinates and three words you can read to the 000 call-taker - ideal on a remote hole.
OHS-02
The evacuation alarm sounds while you are halfway through grinding a cutting unit. What do you do?
Finish the grind first so the unit is not left half done
Drive your Workman out so it does not get damaged by fire
Grinder off if it takes seconds, then go to assembly point
Wait a minute or two to find out whether it is a real emergency
C
When the alarm goes, go. Only make things safe if it takes seconds, and never stop for belongings or vehicles.
OHS-02
At the assembly point you realise Dave, who was working alone on the 17th, is not there. What should you do?
Tell the warden at once so emergency services know where he was last
Drive out to the 17th and look for him yourself before anyone panics
Assume he has already gone home and say nothing about it
Wait until everyone is back at work, then mention it to the Crew Lead
A
Report missing people to the warden at once. Nobody goes back in to search - emergency services do that.
OHS-02
During an evacuation, a warden tells a contractor and a manager to move to the clubhouse assembly point. Who has to follow the instruction?
Only the crew - managers make their own call
Only Club employees - contractors follow their boss
Nobody, unless the Course Superintendent agrees
Everyone - wardens come before normal job roles
D
In an emergency, warden instructions take precedence over the normal management structure. That includes managers, contractors and visitors.
OHS-02
You smell gas near the shed. Which of these should you NOT do?
Keep everyone well away from the area
Turn off the gas at the meter if it is safe
Switch the lights on to help find the leak
Call 000 once you are well away from it
C
Electrical switches and devices can spark and ignite gas. No flames, no switches - get people away and call from a safe distance.
OHS-02
After heavy rain, water is flowing across the track to the 12th. You are in a Workman. What do you do?
Drive through slowly in a low gear range
Turn back - find another route or wait
Walk across first to check the depth
Follow a heavier vehicle through it
B
Floodwater hides washed-out ground and debris, and about 15 cm of flowing water can float a car. Never drive, ride or walk into it.
OHS-02
The fire brigade has put out a small shed fire. You want to grab your phone from the lunchroom. When can you go back in?
When the chief warden gives the all clear
Straight away, now the fire is completely out
As long as you are quick and take a mate
Once the smoke has cleared from the door
A
Nobody goes back in until the chief warden gives the all clear - and if emergency services attended, the chief warden waits for theirs.
OHS-03
A workmate has collapsed near the 12th tee. He does not respond and is making the odd gasping breath. What do you do?
Put him on his side and wait to see if he improves
Start CPR - gasping is not normal breathing
Give him some water and sit him up against a tree
Wait for a trained first aider before doing anything
B
Unresponsive and not breathing normally means start CPR. Occasional gasps are not normal breathing.
OHS-03
You are doing CPR on an adult. Which is right?
About 60 a minute, pressing 2 cm deep
Only start once the ambulance is on the phone
Stop every 30 seconds to check for a pulse
100-120 a minute, a third of the chest depth
D
Push hard and fast - 100 to 120 a minute, about a third of the chest depth (more than 5 cm in an adult) - and keep pauses short.
OHS-03
CPR has started on a workmate. Someone arrives with an AED, but nobody there has used one before. What now?
Keep CPR going, turn the AED on and follow its prompts
Stop CPR and wait for a first aider to work the AED
Leave the AED in its case until paramedics take over
Only use the AED once the person starts breathing again
A
CPR is the key action - keep it going. If an AED is available, anyone can use it: turn it on and follow the prompts.
OHS-03
You are calling 000 for a greenkeeper injured on the 15th. What location details should you give?
Just "Ranfurlie Golf Club" - they will find it
Your home suburb and the name of your boss
The address, the hole and spot, and the gate
Only the nearest hospital and how to get there
C
The street address alone is not enough on a golf course. Give the address, the hole and spot, and which gate you will meet them at.
OHS-03
An ambulance is on its way to a crew member on a remote hole. What else should happen?
Everyone goes to the patient so nobody misses anything
Someone meets it at the gate and leads it in
The patient is driven to the car park to save time
The radio is switched off so the 000 line stays clear
B
Send someone with a radio and hi-vis to the gate to open it and lead the ambulance to the patient. Paramedics decide how the patient is moved.
OHS-03
A golf ball hits Sam on the head. He is dazed for a minute, then says he is fine. What should happen?
He has a drink of water and keeps raking
He takes the rest of the day off and drives home
He goes back to work if he can walk in a straight line
He stops work, is watched closely and 000 is called
D
Being dazed is a warning sign of a significant head injury. He stays still, is monitored, and does not go back to work until a health professional checks him.
OHS-03
A workmate has a deep cut to the forearm from a cutting unit and it is bleeding heavily. What is the first thing to do?
Press firmly and directly on the wound
Lift the arm up and wait for it to slow
Wash the wound under the hose first
Pile on pads until the blood stops showing
A
Firm, direct pressure stops most bleeding. If it soaks through, add one more pad and press harder rather than piling on pads. Call 000.
OHS-03
Lisa is stung by a bee. Her voice goes hoarse and her throat feels tight. She has her own adrenaline auto-injector. What should you do?
Walk her back to the shed so she can sit in the shade
Give her an antihistamine from the first aid kit
Lay her flat, help her use her auto-injector, call 000
Wait 20 minutes and see whether the swelling goes down
C
These are signs of anaphylaxis. Lay her flat (sitting if breathing is hard), do not let her walk, help with her own auto-injector, and call 000.
OHS-03
A crew member falls off a trailer and says his neck hurts. Nothing else is dangerous nearby. What should you do?
Help him up and walk him slowly to the Workman
Get him to turn his head side to side to check it
Sit him up against the trailer so he can breathe
Keep him still, do not move him, and call 000
D
Treat it as a possible spinal injury. Do not move him unless he is in danger. Keep him still and call 000.
OHS-03
A crew member loses the tip of a finger in a cutting unit. After first aid, what else must happen?
Management notifies WorkSafe at once; report it in #ohs
Nothing more - a fingertip is too minor to need reporting
Clean the unit straight away and put it back into service
Leave it until the toolbox talk at the end of the week
A
An amputation is a notifiable incident - WorkSafe must be told immediately. Leave the scene as it is and report it the same day.
OHS-04
A UBIMET lightning alert comes in while you are raking a bunker on the 14th. The sky above you is still blue. What do you do?
Keep raking until you hear the first thunder
Stop, radio the crew, go to shelter
Finish this bunker, then head to the shed
Wait for a second alert before you move
B
Act on the alert - lightning can strike well ahead of the storm. If you hear thunder or see lightning before an alert, shelter anyway and radio it.
OHS-04
Which of these is lightning-safe shelter?
Under a big gum tree beside the fairway
In a Workman with a canopy roof fitted
A hard-top ute with the windows up
Any course extreme weather shelter
C
Only a solid, fully enclosed building or a hard-top, fully enclosed vehicle is safe. The weather shelters are not lightning shelter unless your supervisor confirms it.
OHS-04
You are in shelter. The last thunder was 20 minutes ago, the rain has stopped and the sun is out. Can you go back to work?
Yes - the sun is out and the rain has stopped
Yes - as long as you keep away from trees
Yes - if the UBIMET alert has gone quiet
No - wait for 30 minutes and the all clear
D
Blue sky is not a reason to go out early. Every new rumble restarts the 30 minutes, and only your supervisor gives the all clear.
OHS-04
You are mowing greens with two passes left when the lightning alert comes through. What should you do?
Shut it down, leave it, get to shelter
Finish the two passes - it takes 3 minutes
Drive the mower to the next green and wait
Lie flat on the green until it passes over
A
Stop straight away. The job can wait. Get off the machine and get to safe shelter.
OHS-04
You are caught in the open by lightning with no shelter you can reach. What should you do?
Lie flat on the ground until it passes
Shelter under the nearest big tree
Hold your rake up so the crew can see you
Crouch low, feet together, tools down
D
Crouch low with your feet together - do not lie flat. Keep away from trees, water, fences and machines, and spread out if you are in a group.
OHS-04
Golfers are still playing the hole next to you when the lightning alert comes in. What is your job?
Clear every golfer off the course yourself
Get to shelter, warning golfers near you
Stay out until every golfer has gone in
Keep working until the golfers go in
B
Clearing golfers is not the crew's job - management arranges it. Warn anyone near you as you go, but do not delay your own move to shelter.
OHS-04
The morning after a storm you find a wire lying across the track and touching the boundary fence. What do you do?
Lift it clear of the track with a dry stick
Drive across it quickly in the Workman
Stay 10 m back, keep people away, radio it
Touch the fence to see whether it is live
C
Treat every fallen powerline as live. Stay at least 10 m from it and anything it touches, call 000 if anyone is in danger, and report it.
OHS-04
After heavy rain, water is flowing over the creek crossing. The long way round adds ten minutes. What do you do?
Go the long way round instead
Drive across slowly in the ute
Wade across first to test the depth
Cross on foot carrying your gear
A
If it's flooded, forget it. Just 15 cm of flowing water can float a car, and the crossing may have washed out underneath.
OHS-04
A co-worker has just been struck by lightning and is not breathing normally. The storm has moved off. What do you do?
Wait 30 minutes in case they are charged
Call 000 and start CPR straight away
Carry them to the shed and let them rest
Pour cold water over them to cool them
B
A person who has been struck does not carry a charge and is safe to touch. Call 000, start CPR and use a defibrillator if one is available.
OHS-04
After a storm, water has got into the pump station and the switchboard is wet. What should happen?
Switch it back on to see if it still works
Dry it with a towel, then switch it on
Leave it off - an electrician must test it
Run the pumps for a minute to clear the water
C
Anything electrical that has been flooded must be tested by a licensed electrician before it is used again. Report it and keep others away.
OHS-05
Is there a maximum temperature in Victoria above which the law says outdoor work must stop?
Yes - work must stop at 35 degrees
Yes - work must stop at 40 degrees
No - but the heat risk must be managed
No - so work always carries on as normal
C
The OHS laws do not set a maximum temperature. The Club must still control the risk, which depends on humidity, sun, workload and PPE, not just temperature.
OHS-05
A bunker rebuild needs a lot of shovelling, and tomorrow is forecast to be 35 degrees and humid. When should the heavy work be done?
Early in the morning, in the cooler part of the day
In the middle of the day, when the sand is dry
In the afternoon, after the greens are cut
Whenever suits - the time of day makes no difference
A
Heavy and hot jobs are scheduled for the cooler part of the day, with lighter or shaded jobs left for later.
OHS-05
How much should you drink while working in the heat?
Only when you start to feel thirsty
A large bottle at lunch and at knock-off
Water every 15 minutes, thirsty or not
Energy drinks whenever you feel flat
C
Drink water every 15 minutes, even if you are not thirsty (about a cup). Thirst kicks in late. Do not rely on soft drinks, energy drinks or coffee.
OHS-05
Why does spraying in full chemical PPE need extra care on hot days?
PPE stops your body sweating at all
It traps heat close to your body
It only matters when spraying herbicide
It does not - PPE keeps the sun off you
B
Coveralls, gloves and respirators trap heat, so heat illness can come on faster. Spray early and take extra breaks - never take off required PPE to cool down.
OHS-05
An apprentice hand-watering greens is stumbling, confused and has red, hot skin. He says he is fine. What do you do?
Let him finish the green, then send him home
Give him an energy drink and watch him
Sit him in his car with the windows up
Call 000 and start cooling him now
D
Confusion and hot skin point to heatstroke - a medical emergency. Call 000, cool him with cold water, ice packs and fanning, and stay with him.
OHS-05
A co-worker is pale, sweating heavily, dizzy and feels sick after raking bunkers. What is the right first aid?
Lie them down somewhere cool and cool them
Tell them to walk it off in the shade
Give salt tablets and send them back out
Leave them to rest on their own in the shed
A
These are signs of heat exhaustion. Cool and rest them, give sips of water, stay with them, and call 000 if they get worse or you suspect heatstroke.
OHS-05
You need to cool someone with heatstroke while waiting for the ambulance. Which of these should you NOT do?
Soak them with cold water from a hose
Ice packs on their neck, armpits and groin
Put them in the dam to cool them down
Fan them continuously while you wait
C
Cool them with cold water, ice packs and fanning. Never put anyone in a lake, dam or creek.
OHS-05
You get painful cramps in your legs while laying turf on a hot day. What should you do?
Push through until the job is finished
Stop, rest in the shade and drink water
Stretch hard and get straight back to it
Take your shirt off to cool and keep going
B
Heat cramps are a warning sign. Stop, rest in a cool place with legs raised, drink cool water and tell your supervisor. Get medical care if they do not ease.
OHS-05
A new starter is in his first week, and it is the first hot day of spring. What should happen?
Give him the heaviest jobs to toughen him up
Let him work alone at his own pace
Nothing extra - heat only affects older staff
Ease him in, check on him, give him a buddy
D
People new to outdoor work are not used to the heat and often push themselves to keep up. Extra checks and a buddy reduce the risk.
OHS-05
A co-worker who has been spraying gets a headache, dizziness and nausea. What should you keep in mind?
It is definitely just the heat - cool them
It could be heat or chemicals - treat both
It is chemical poisoning, so do not cool them
These symptoms always pass on their own
B
These signs can come from heat or chemical exposure. Stop the job, follow the decontamination steps in CHM-05, cool them and tell your supervisor.
OHS-06
Which fire weather district do you check for Ranfurlie when looking up the Fire Danger Rating or a Total Fire Ban?
South West district
Central district
North Central district
Mallee district
B
Ranfurlie is in the City of Casey, which is in the Central fire weather district. Check it on the VicEmergency app or the CFA website.
OHS-06
It is a Total Fire Ban day and a mower bracket needs welding. The mechanic wants to do it in the yard outside the shed. What should happen?
Go ahead if a hose is connected nearby
Go ahead before 10 am while it is cool
No - outdoor hot work is banned today
Go ahead if someone stands by with water
C
Welding, grinding and cutting in the open air are banned on TFB days. Our rule: no hot work outdoors - the mower stays tagged out.
OHS-06
The job board has slashing the dry native grass along the boundary, and a Total Fire Ban has been declared. What do you do?
Check with your supervisor - it comes off
Slash it early before the day heats up
Slash it, carrying a dry-powder extinguisher
Slash it quickly so it is done by lunch
A
Our rule is no mowing, trimming or slashing of dry grass on TFB days. CFA also says avoid using machinery wherever possible on those days.
OHS-06
During the Fire Danger Period you need to use a line trimmer in dry grass. Which fire equipment must you carry?
Nothing - line trimmers are exempt
A bucket of sand and a long shovel
A small dry-powder fire extinguisher
A 9 L knapsack or water extinguisher
D
In dry grass the machine must be fault-free with a spark arrester, 3 m cleared around it, and the operator must carry at least 9 litres of water.
OHS-06
Why should you never park a ute or Workman on long dry grass in summer?
It leaves deep tyre ruts in the turf
The hot exhaust can ignite the grass
Golfers might hit it with a stray ball
The crew may not be able to find it
B
Exhausts, catalytic converters and particulate filters run hot enough to ignite dry grass. Park on paths, bitumen, concrete or irrigated turf.
OHS-06
It is a Total Fire Ban day. Which barbecue can the crew use for lunch?
Charcoal kettle, if a hose is nearby
Wood-fired pizza oven, if attended
Gas barbecue, with all conditions met
Any barbecue, as long as it is on concrete
C
Solid-fuel and liquid-fuel cooking is banned on TFB days. A gas or electric barbecue needs 3 m cleared, 10 L of water or a hose, and an adult attending.
OHS-06
You see smoke rising from dry grass near your machine and the fire is starting to spread in the wind. What do you do?
Beat it out with your hat or jacket
Drive the Workman over it to flatten it
Wait to see whether it burns itself out
Raise the alarm, call 000, get away
D
Never fight a fire that is spreading. Grassfires can move faster than you can run. Raise the alarm, call 000 and get to safety.
OHS-06
When is a Total Fire Ban usually announced, and how long does it last?
Afternoon before; midnight to midnight
That morning; it runs from 9 am to 5 pm
A week ahead; it runs for the whole week
When a fire starts; until it is put out
A
TFBs are usually declared the afternoon before and apply from midnight to midnight. Check VicEmergency or the CFA website.
OHS-06
During the Fire Danger Period, the crew finds a pile of fallen branches. Can someone burn it?
Yes - on a cool, still, damp morning
Yes - if someone stays to watch it
No - it needs a permit, via management
Yes - if it is in the middle of a fairway
C
Burning off without a permit during the FDP is illegal, and staff never burn off - management arranges any permit. On TFB days it is banned even with a permit.
OHS-06
The forecast for tomorrow is Catastrophic for the Central district. What should you expect?
Normal work, with extra water and breaks
Normal work, but spraying is cancelled
Normal work, finishing 30 minutes early
Essential jobs only, or no outdoor work
D
On Catastrophic days lives are likely to be lost if a fire takes hold. The Course Superintendent decides the day before and posts the plan in #course-team.
OHS-07
A small fire starts in a tray of spilled petrol in the workshop. Which extinguisher must you NOT use?
ABE powder extinguisher
Foam extinguisher
Water extinguisher
BE powder extinguisher
C
Water spreads burning fuel. Use dry chemical powder or foam on fuel and oil fires.
OHS-07
A battery charger on the workshop bench is sparking and has caught fire. It is still small. What is right?
Throw a bucket of water over it straight away
Use the foam extinguisher - it smothers the flames
Wait for it to burn out, then unplug it
Power off if safe, then use CO2 or dry powder
D
Never use water or foam on live electrical equipment. Switch off if safe and use CO2 or dry chemical powder.
OHS-07
You are using an extinguisher on a small fire. Where do you aim it?
At the base of the fire
At the top of the flames
Into the smoke above it
At the wall behind the fire
A
PASS - Pull the pin, Aim at the base of the fire, Squeeze the handle, Sweep side to side.
OHS-07
Smoke and small flames are coming from under the engine cover of your mower. You have stopped, turned the engine off and got clear. If you fight it, how?
Lift the engine cover right up and spray inside
Release the catch only and spray through the gap
Pour a drink bottle of water into the engine bay
Restart the engine to blow the flames out
B
Lifting the cover lets in a rush of air that can make the fire flare. Release the catch only and spray through the gap - or get well away.
OHS-07
A fire in the shed is spreading and is now between you and the door you came in. What do you do?
Grab a second extinguisher and try to finish it off
Keep fighting it, since you have already got started
Leave by another exit, close doors and call 000
Open the windows first so that the smoke can clear
C
Only tackle a fire if you have a clear way out behind you. If one extinguisher does not put it out, it is too big - get out.
OHS-07
On your monthly check, an extinguisher has its pin missing and the gauge needle is in the red. What should you do?
Report it to your supervisor straight away
Put a new cable tie through it and leave it
Tap the gauge until the needle moves up
Leave it - the six-monthly service will pick it up
A
A missing pin or low gauge means it may not work. Report it straight away so it is serviced or replaced.
OHS-07
Last week you used part of the workshop extinguisher on a small rag fire and the fire went out. What should have happened?
Hang it back up - there is plenty left
Report it so it is recharged or replaced
Shake it and test it again before rehanging
Only report it if more than half was used
B
Report any use, even a short burst, so it is recharged or replaced - and report the fire as an incident.
OHS-07
During an evacuation drill, a warden tells a visiting contractor to move to the assembly point. He says he only takes orders from his own boss. Who is right?
The contractor - wardens only direct Club staff
Neither - everyone should decide for themselves
The contractor, unless it is a genuine emergency
The warden - everyone must follow the warden
D
In an emergency or drill, warden instructions come before normal management. That includes managers, contractors and visitors.
OHS-07
How often does the Club have a competent person inspect and service its extinguishers?
Every six months, following AS 1851
Every five years, when it is refilled
Only after it has been used on a fire
Only when the gauge drops into the red
A
Club practice is six-monthly inspection and servicing by a competent person, following AS 1851, plus yearly and five-yearly servicing. Each service is recorded on the tag.
OHS-08
You are mowing a green when a hydraulic hose bursts and oil sprays onto the turf. What do you do first?
Finish the pass so the oil is not left mid-green
Stop, reels off, engine off, radio your supervisor
Hose the oil off with the nearest quick-coupler
Drive straight back to the workshop for a repair
B
Driving on spreads the oil and the damage. Stop, shut down, warn the crew, then blot the oil with pads.
OHS-08
Diesel is running across the fuel bay concrete towards a stormwater pit. After making it safe, what comes first?
Cover the pit, then contain and absorb
Hose the diesel away from the shed doors
Leave it to evaporate and mention it at smoko
Spread granules once it has reached the pit
A
Stormwater pits lead to creeks and the bay, not a treatment plant. Protect the drain first, then work from the outside in.
OHS-08
A hydraulic hose on a Workman is weeping. How do you find exactly where it is leaking?
Run your bare hand along the hose, engine running
Squeeze each fitting with a rag while it is idling
Hold your face close to the hose and look for mist
Shut down, tag it out, report it to the workshop
D
A pinhole leak under pressure can inject fluid through the skin - a serious injury. Tag the machine out (OHS-14) and let the workshop find the leak safely.
OHS-08
A fuel sheen is floating at the edge of a lake. Which absorbent is best for soaking it up?
Chemical/hazmat pads thrown out onto the lake
Detergent sprayed on the water to break it up
Oil-only pads or boom, used from the bank
Loose granules scattered over the water
C
Oil-only absorbent repels water, so it picks up fuel and oil floating on water. Work from the bank - never go into the water. Detergent just spreads it.
OHS-08
You have finished cleaning up a small oil spill in the workshop. What happens to the used pads?
Into the general rubbish bin in the shed
Bagged, labelled, into the spill waste bin
Onto the green waste pile with the clippings
Dropped at the local tip on the way home
B
In Victoria, absorbent contaminated with hazardous substances is reportable priority waste. It must go to a licensed contractor via a permitted transporter.
OHS-08
Which of these spills means you should get clear and call 000?
A cup of coolant on the workshop floor
A few drops of two-stroke mix at the bowser
A torn bag of granular fertiliser on the shed floor
A large petrol spill in the shed, strong vapour
D
Fire risk, strong vapour in an enclosed space, injuries or a spill you cannot control safely - get clear, keep others back and call 000.
OHS-08
Tank mix from a split sprayer hose has run into a stormwater pit that drains to a creek. What happens next?
Nothing - it was only diluted tank mix anyway
Hose the pit out so it flushes through quickly
Tell your supervisor now - EPA may need to know
Mention it at the next weekly toolbox talk
C
A spill that causes or threatens material harm to the environment must be notified to EPA as soon as practicable. Report it straight away so management can act.
OHS-08
Battery acid splashes onto your forearm while you are moving a cart battery. What should you do?
Wipe it off with a dry rag, cover it with a clean dressing and keep moving the batteries
Flush with running water at least 20 minutes (up to an hour, until stinging stops); call 000
Pour baking soda over the arm to neutralise the acid, then rinse it off with a little water
Rinse it under the tap for about 30 seconds, put a bandage on it and finish the job first
B
For chemical burns, ANZCOR says flush for at least 20 minutes and send for an ambulance. Never try to neutralise acid on skin.
OHS-08
You need to clean up a spilled chemical. Which part of the SDS tells you how?
Section 6 - Accidental release measures
Section 7 - Handling and storage
Section 11 - Toxicological information
Section 13 - Disposal considerations
A
Section 6 covers containing and cleaning up a spill. Section 8 tells you the PPE to wear while you do it.
OHS-08
You have just used half the pads from the spill kit in the shed. What should you do?
Nothing - there are still some pads left
Top it up with pads from the sprayer kit
Buy a bag of shop rags on the way home tonight
Tell your supervisor and report it in #ohs
D
A half-empty kit is not much use in the next emergency. Every use is reported (#ohs and the form) and the kit is restocked.
OHS-09
Two degreasers are on the shelf. One label says DANGER, the other says WARNING. What does that tell you?
They mean the same - both are just warnings
The DANGER product has the more severe hazard
The WARNING product has the more severe hazard
DANGER only applies if the product is heated
B
GHS signal words show severity: DANGER is used for more severe hazards, WARNING for less severe ones.
OHS-09
You are about to use a new cleaner and want to know what gloves and eye protection to wear. Which SDS section do you check?
Section 2 - Hazard identification
Section 6 - Accidental release measures
Section 8 - Personal protection
Section 13 - Disposal considerations
C
Section 8 (exposure controls and personal protection) lists the PPE. Section 4 is first aid, section 6 is spills, section 7 is storage.
OHS-09
You need a small amount of degreaser in a spray bottle for the workshop. What is the rule?
Nothing, as long as you remember what is in it now
Reuse an empty drink bottle - they are easy to grip
Write CHEMICAL on the side in permanent marker
Label it with the product name; never a drink bottle
D
The law requires decanted containers to carry the product name unless used and cleaned immediately. WorkSafe guidance says never use food or drink containers.
OHS-09
You find an unlabelled drink bottle with blue liquid in it on a workshop bench. What should you do?
Set it aside safely and tell your supervisor
Take the lid off and smell it to work out what it is
Tip it down the wash bay drain so nobody drinks it
Use it up on the next suitable job so it is gone
A
An unknown chemical could be anything. Make sure nobody drinks from it, and your supervisor arranges disposal as chemical waste.
OHS-09
A sales rep leaves a free sample of a new product in the shed. What happens before anyone uses it?
Nothing - free samples are exempt from the rules
SDS obtained and register updated before use
Try a small amount first to see how it works
Store it in the chemical store and use it next week
B
The Club must have a current SDS on or before first supply and keep the register up to date. New products are checked before use.
OHS-09
A pallet of nitrate-based fertiliser has been stacked next to the jerry cans of petrol. Why is that a problem?
It is not - fertiliser is not a chemical
The fertiliser will make the petrol go stale
Some nitrates are oxidisers that feed fires
Petrol fumes will stop the fertiliser working
C
Oxidisers make fires start more easily and burn fiercer, so they are kept away from fuels. Check SDS sections 7 and 10 and move it.
OHS-09
Why must lead-acid batteries be charged only in the ventilated charging area, away from sparks?
Charging gives off explosive hydrogen gas
Charging can make the battery acid freeze
Fresh air helps the battery charge faster
It only keeps dust off the battery terminals
A
Charging lead-acid batteries releases hydrogen. Ventilation and keeping sparks and flames away prevent an explosion.
OHS-09
The signal heading on a pesticide label reads DANGEROUS POISON. What does that tell you?
It is the lowest of the scheduled levels
The most serious level; needs an ACUP holder
It only applies to products used on animals
The product is not registered for turf use
B
Scheduled headings are CAUTION, POISON and DANGEROUS POISON (most serious). Only ACUP holders, or someone under their direct and immediate supervision (within sight and sound), may use them.
OHS-09
You notice the SDS in the folder for a herbicide we use is dated 2018. What should you do?
Nothing - an SDS never really goes out of date
Cross out the date and write in today's date
Throw it out so nobody reads the old information
Ask your supervisor to get a current one
D
WorkSafe guidance says the SDS held should be dated within the last five years. Never alter an SDS - get a current one.
OHS-09
A chemical splashes in your eye. What is the first aid?
Rub the eye gently and keep on working
Use normal eye drops and wait for an hour
Eyewash for at least 15 minutes, lids open
Rinse it briefly, then finish the job first
C
Flush straight away for at least 15 minutes (longer for corrosives), then call 13 11 26 or get medical help - 000 for corrosives. Full steps are in CHM-05.
OHS-11
Is there a legal maximum weight a worker can lift in Victoria?
Yes - 25 kg for one person lifting alone
Yes - 20 kg, and 16 kg for apprentices
No - the law sets no weight limit
Yes - whatever weight is printed on the bag
C
There is no legal weight limit - risk depends on posture, distance, force and frequency too. A 4 kg load at arm's length can take as much effort as 12 kg held close.
OHS-11
You need to swap a cutting unit on a greens mower and nobody else is around. What do you do?
Isolate it and use the hoist, or wait for help
Lift it off by hand, keeping your back straight
Drag it off the mower and onto a rubber mat
Lift it off with a passing golfer helping you
A
Cutting units are heavy and awkward with pinch points. Isolate first (OHS-15), then use an aid or a planned two-person lift. Never lift one by hand alone.
OHS-11
You are planning a heavy, repetitive job. Which control should you look at first?
Training everyone in good lifting technique
Rotating the job between several workers
Removing the handling or changing the job
Doing a proper warm-up before you start
C
Work down the order: eliminate, change the job, mechanical aids, team lifts, rotation, then technique. Technique is the last line.
OHS-11
A pallet of 20 kg fertiliser bags is on the shed floor and you need to fill the spreader. What is the best approach?
Lift each bag off the pallet and tip it in
Move them at waist height on a trolley or tray
Carry two bags at once so you make fewer trips
Hoist each bag onto your shoulder and walk it
B
Use an aid, work at waist height and slide rather than lift. Lifting from the floor and twisting is a classic way to hurt your back.
OHS-11
After three mornings on the line trimmer, your fingers tingle and go numb. What should you do?
Nothing - tingling usually passes after a day
Grip the trimmer harder to cut the vibration
Keep going and mention it if it starts to hurt
Report it to your supervisor the same day
D
Tingling and numbness can be early signs of vibration injury. Report it the same day in #ohs and on the form so the job can be changed.
OHS-11
You and a mate are doing a team lift of a heavy valve out of a pit. Which is right?
One person calls it and you lift and lower together
Each person lifts as soon as they feel ready
The stronger person quietly takes most of the weight
Each person lets go as soon as they get tired
A
Team lifts need one person in charge, a clear route, an agreed call and moving together. Nobody lets go without warning.
OHS-11
Hand watering a green, your hose snags on a sprinkler head behind you. What should you do?
Give it one hard yank to pop it free
Twist round and pull it free with one arm
Flick the hose sideways until it comes loose
Walk back to the head and free it by hand
D
Jerking a snagged hose is a sudden, high force in an awkward posture. Walk back, free it, and lay the hose to avoid heads next time.
OHS-11
Why is job rotation only a stop-gap control?
It costs too much to run long term
It does not remove the source of the risk
It is not allowed under the OHS Regulations
It only works with crews of four or more
B
Rotation cuts exposure time and lets muscles recover, but the hazardous task is still there. Fix the job itself where you can.
OHS-11
When is it OK to rely only on good lifting technique?
When higher controls aren't reasonably practicable
Always - it is the most effective control there is
For any load lighter than 20 kg printed on the bag
Whenever an aid would take too long to fetch
A
Information, training and technique come last. Rely on them alone only when eliminating, changing the job and mechanical aids are not reasonably practicable.
OHS-11
You hurt your back lifting a wet roll of turf. What should you do?
Keep working and see if it settles by tomorrow
Go home early and tell your supervisor next week
Stop, report it today and get it checked
Only report it if you end up needing time off
C
Stop, tell your supervisor, report it in #ohs and on the incident form, and see a doctor if needed. You may be entitled to WorkCover.
OHS-13
A golf ball lands two metres from you while you are changing a hole. Nobody is hurt. What is it, and what do you do?
Nothing to report, because nobody was hurt
A near miss - move clear, then #ohs and the form
An incident - phone WorkSafe on 13 23 60 straight away
A hazard - put a cone on the green and carry on
B
Something that could have hurt someone but did not is a near miss. Near misses are reported the same way as everything else.
OHS-13
What are the two steps for every report?
Tell a co-worker and post it on the crew chat
Email WorkSafe and tell your supervisor next week
Write it on the shed whiteboard and wait
Post in #ohs and complete the notice-board form
D
Every hazard, near miss, incident and injury goes in #ohs (a photo helps) and on the form from the staff notice board, the same shift.
OHS-13
A mower is leaking hydraulic oil onto a green and the hose looks ready to burst. What comes first?
Stop it, keep people clear and tell your supervisor
Post a photo in #ohs, then finish mowing the green
Finish the green quickly, then report the leak after
Fill in the form first, then decide what to do
A
If it is dangerous right now, make it safe if you can and tell your supervisor straight away. Then post in #ohs and do the form.
OHS-13
Spray mix splashes on a crew member's arm. They wash it off, keep working, and see a GP the next day about a rash. Why does this matter?
It does not matter - they washed it off straight away
It only matters if they need time off work
It is a notifiable incident - WorkSafe must be told
It only needs to be noted in the spray records
C
Medical treatment within 48 hours of exposure to a substance must be notified to WorkSafe. Report splashes the same shift.
OHS-13
A Workman has tipped over on a bank. The driver is out and unhurt. What should happen to the vehicle?
Right it straight away so the bank can be finished
Leave it, keep people clear, tell your supervisor
Drive it back to the shed and check it over
Photograph it and post the photos in the crew chat
B
The scene is left as it is except to help an injured person or make it safe. Management decides whether WorkSafe must be notified - an overturn can be notifiable even if nobody is hurt.
OHS-13
What number does management call to notify WorkSafe of a notifiable incident?
D
Notifiable incidents go to WorkSafe on 13 23 60, 24/7, immediately. 1800 136 089 is the Advisory Service for general questions.
OHS-13
After phoning WorkSafe about a notifiable incident, when must the written notification be sent?
Within 48 hours
Within 72 hours
Within 30 days
Within 14 days
A
Written notification is due within 48 hours, and a copy is kept for at least 5 years.
OHS-13
You strain your back lifting bags of sand. It is sore but you finish the job. When should you report it?
Only if you end up needing time off
Any time in the next 30 days is fine
Before the end of your shift
At your next performance review
C
The Club rule is to report injuries the same shift - tell your supervisor, post briefly in #ohs and do the form. Small injuries can get worse.
OHS-13
You clip an irrigation head with a mower and crack it. You worry you will get in trouble. What should you do?
Report it - honest reports are no-blame
Say nothing and hope that nobody notices
Blame whoever used the mower before you
Fix it yourself quietly once the crew has gone
A
You will not be punished for reporting an honest mistake. Hiding incidents is the bigger problem, and it stops us fixing the cause.
OHS-13
A crew member feels a co-worker keeps putting him down in front of the crew. How should he raise it?
Post the details in #ohs so everyone knows
Ignore it - it is not a safety issue
Confront the co-worker in front of the crew
Tell his supervisor or a manager privately
D
Psychosocial hazards like bullying can and should be reported, but privately - not in #ohs. They are handled confidentially under OHS-32.
OHS-19
You are about to head out alone to hand-water the back nine. What must your supervisor know before you go?
Nothing - TurfDog already shows your jobs
The job, where, finish time and check-ins
Only which machine you are taking out
Only the time you expect to finish
B
Someone must always know what you are doing, where you are and when you will be done, and you agree check-in times before you start.
OHS-19
Which check-in pattern does this procedure recommend as a default?
At the start and again at lunch only
Every 4 hours, plus when you finish
Start, about every 2 hours, and finish
Only when you change holes or change jobs
C
Check in at the start, about every 2 hours (more often in heat, the dark or higher-risk work), when you change area or job, and before you leave site.
OHS-19
A pump intake in a pond is blocked. You could wade in and clear it in five minutes. What do you do?
Radio your supervisor for a second person
Clear it quickly, then check in straight after
Go in, as long as you are a confident swimmer
Leave your phone on the bank and wade in
A
Work in or right next to water is on the never-alone list. You could get stuck or be unable to climb out with nobody to help.
OHS-19
You are whipper-snipping a steep bank on a remote hole. Where should your phone be?
In the cup holder of the cart
In your bag back at the shed
On the seat of the Workman
On you, in a pocket or belt
D
If you are thrown, trapped or injured, you need to reach your phone and radio. Keep both on your body, charged.
OHS-19
A crew member misses their 9am check-in. What is the first step?
Wait until lunch - they probably forgot
Call 000 straight away and start a search
Radio them, then call their mobile
Post a message about it in #ohs and wait
C
Start with radio then mobile. If there is no answer, ask the crew, send someone to their last known location and escalate on the timeline.
OHS-19
During a search for someone who missed a check-in, you find their mower overturned near a pond. What do you do?
Call 000 straight away and keep searching
Wait until the 30-minute mark to call 000
Right the mower before doing anything else
Drive back to the shed to get more help
A
Any sign of an accident means call 000 immediately - do not wait for the timeline.
OHS-19
After a storm, a large branch is down across a path. You have a chainsaw ticket, but nobody else is around. What do you do?
Cut it up - you have a chainsaw ticket
Cut it up, then check in when you finish
Ask a passing golfer to stand nearby
Tape it off and wait for a second person
D
Chainsaw and tree work is never done alone. The second person keeps the drop zone clear and can get help fast if something goes wrong.
OHS-19
You need to go into a part of the course with no radio or mobile coverage. What should you do?
Just go - you will not be in there for long
Check in before and after, giving a time
Turn your radio off to save the battery
Only go in when it is full daylight outside
B
Blackspots break the check-in system. Check in before you go, say when you will be back in range, check in again when you are, and report new blackspots in #ohs.
OHS-19
What do Victoria's Psychological Health Regulations say about remote or isolated work?
Nothing - they only cover bullying
It is banned for all employees
It is a listed psychosocial hazard
It only applies to office workers
C
Since 1 December 2025 employers must identify and control psychosocial hazards, and remote or isolated work is one of them.
OHS-27
You see a snake on the bunker face of the 3rd as golfers walk up the fairway. What do you do?
Kill it with the rake before it bites someone
Back away, keep golfers back, radio it in
Lift it into the rough with a long shovel
Throw sand at it until it slides away
B
Never try to catch, move or kill a snake - most bites happen that way and snakes are protected. Keep people away and report it.
OHS-27
A co-worker feels a scratch on her ankle in long rough and sees a snake slide away. There is no pain. What do you do?
Wash the bite and keep working if no pain
Walk her to the shed and watch her closely
Keep her still, call 000, bandage the leg
Tie a tight tourniquet above the bite
C
A snake bite can be painless with only a scratch. Keep the person still, call 000, apply a pressure immobilisation bandage and splint, and bring the vehicle to them.
OHS-27
Which of these should you NOT do for a snake bite on the leg?
Wash the bite site with water
Keep the person lying down and still
Bandage firmly from the toes upwards
Splint the leg, including the knee
A
Do not wash, cut or suck the bite, and do not use a tourniquet. Bandage the whole limb, splint it and keep the person still.
OHS-27
Someone has been bitten by a redback spider in the shed. What is the right first aid?
A firm pressure immobilisation bandage
A cold pack; medical care if severe
Wash the bite, then suck out the venom
A tourniquet tied above the bite site
B
Pressure bandages are not used for redback bites - they make the pain worse. Use a cold pack, watch them, and get medical care if pain is severe or they collapse.
OHS-27
Wasps from a valve box sting you several times on the face, and your lips start to swell. What do you do?
Keep working - some swelling is normal
Take a painkiller and finish the repair
Wash your face and wait an hour to see
Get clear, call 000 and lie down
D
Swelling of the face, lips or throat can be anaphylaxis. Get away from the nest, lie down, use your autoinjector if you have one and call 000.
OHS-27
A co-worker with a known bee allergy is stung and is wheezing. Which first aid is correct?
Walk them back to the shed to sit down
Keep them still, use adrenaline, call 000
Give a cold drink and see if it settles down
Sit them in the sun and let them rest
B
For anaphylaxis, keep them lying flat (or sitting if breathing is hard), give their adrenaline autoinjector and call 000. Do not let them stand or walk.
OHS-27
An apprentice finds an injured bat on the shed floor and wants to put it in a box. What should happen?
Pick it up in a rag so it cannot bite
Pick it up with gloves and put it outside
Do not touch it - call Wildlife Victoria
Sweep it gently out the door with a broom
C
Any bat could carry Australian bat lyssavirus. Only trained, vaccinated people handle bats. If bitten or scratched, wash for 15 minutes and see a doctor urgently.
OHS-27
You find one dead duck at the edge of a course lake. What do you do?
Leave it, photo it, tell a supervisor
Bag it and put it in the general bin
Bury it in the rough away from golfers
Ignore it - only large die-offs matter
A
Even one dead waterbird is reported to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline (1800 675 888) because of H5 bird flu. Do not touch it.
OHS-27
A sore on your forearm started as a painless lump and is not healing after several weeks. What should you do?
Ignore it - it is only an insect bite
Squeeze it, then cover it with a plaster
Put insect repellent on it each morning
See a GP and mention your outdoor work
D
Buruli ulcer often starts as a painless lump mistaken for a bite, and occurs in the nearby Frankston/Langwarrin region. Early diagnosis matters.
OHS-27
A magpie keeps swooping you near the 7th tee in spring. What is the best approach?
Throw something at it to scare it off
Knock down the nest once the bird has gone
Avoid it; if you must pass, walk calmly
Sprint through the area as fast as you can
C
Magpies swoop to protect their young. Avoid the area, move calmly with a hat on, tell your supervisor, and never harass the bird or its nest.
OHS-28
Three of you need to get to the 14th and the Workman only has two seats. What do you do?
One person rides in the tray, holding on
Make two trips, or one person walks over
One person stands on the step and holds on
Two people squeeze into the passenger seat
B
Passengers only ride in a proper seat, one per seat. Trays, steps and trailers are never for people.
OHS-28
How fast should you drive near the shed, around people and in the car park?
The posted road speed limit for the area
Top speed, if the path ahead looks clear
Whatever speed keeps the job on schedule
Walking pace - slow enough to stop
D
People on foot can step out at any time. Walking pace gives you time to stop.
OHS-28
You are reversing a trailer into the shed and cannot see behind it. What should you do?
Use a spotter and stop if you lose sight
Reverse slowly and rely on the reversing beeper
Toot the horn twice and keep reversing slowly
Lean out the side and reverse in short bursts
A
A beeper does not replace looking. If you cannot see, use a spotter, agree signals first, and stop the moment you lose sight of them.
OHS-28
You stop the Gator to fix a sprinkler. How should you leave it?
Engine running so you can get going quickly
Key left in so others can move it if needed
Level ground, brake on, engine off, key out
Wherever is handy, as long as it is in gear
C
Level ground, brake on, engine off and key out stops it rolling and stops anyone else - including the public - using it.
OHS-28
Your phone rings while you are driving across the 6th fairway. What do you do?
Answer on speaker and keep driving slowly
Pull over and stop before you answer it
Glance at it at the next crossing, still moving
Answer it as long as no golfers are nearby
B
No calls, texts or apps while driving. Pull over and stop first - it takes seconds.
OHS-28
A mower is needed on the other side of a public road. It is only a few hundred metres. What is the rule?
Drive it across quickly with the hazard lights on
Drive it - mowers never need registration
Drive it along the footpath instead of the road
Only if the Superintendent says it is permitted
D
Mowers and carts are only exempt in narrow conditions and must not use footpaths. The Superintendent must confirm it is registered or permitted and you are licensed.
OHS-28
The seatbelt alarm on a side-by-side keeps beeping. A mate says to clip the belt behind the seat. What do you do?
Clip it behind the seat - it is a short trip
Pull the fuse so the alarm stops beeping
Wear the seatbelt and leave the alarm alone
Only wear it when you are driving on slopes
C
Never bypass safety features - on some side-by-sides it also overrides the speed limiter. The belt keeps you inside the ROPS zone in a rollover.
OHS-28
Early morning, heavy dew. You need to check a pump next to the dam at the bottom of a grassy bank. What should you do?
Park well back from the edge and walk down
Drive straight down the bank to save time
Drive along the dam edge where it is flatter
Coast down the bank in neutral to keep it slow
A
Dew cuts grip and edges can collapse. Never coast downhill in neutral. If in doubt, park on safe ground and walk.
OHS-28
You clip a member's parked cart with the Workman. Nobody is hurt and there is only a small scratch. What do you do?
Nothing - it is only a small scratch
Tell the member yourself and leave it there
Touch it up quietly before anyone notices
Tell your supervisor and report it in #ohs
D
Report every incident and near miss, even minor ones, in #ohs and on the incident form. Reports help fix the cause before someone gets hurt.
OHS-28
You are loading the Workman tray with sand bags and tools. Which is right?
Load it as high as it goes to save a trip
Leave the tailgate down so it unloads easier
Stay within the limit and tie it all down
Put the heaviest items right at the back
C
Loads change braking and stability, especially on slopes. Stay within limits, secure the load, keep heavy items low and centred, and keep the tailgate up.
OHS-31
You had a few drinks at a party and got to bed at 1am. You start on the greens mower at 5am. What is right?
You are fine to start if you feel OK
It is 0.00 - tell your supervisor first
You are fine if you are under 0.05
A strong coffee will clear it before 5am
B
Zero alcohol applies from the start of your shift. Alcohol can still be in your system next morning, and coffee or cold showers do not speed it up.
OHS-31
Your hay fever tablet says "may cause drowsiness - if affected, do not drive or operate machinery". What do you do?
Take it and keep mowing - it is only hay fever
Stop taking it and say nothing to anyone
Tell your supervisor it may make you drowsy
Take it, but only mow the flat areas
C
Label warnings apply to our machines. Tell your supervisor it may affect you - you do not need to share your condition - and ask your pharmacist about alternatives.
OHS-31
Do you have to tell your supervisor what medical condition your medicine is for?
No - just that it may affect you, and how
Yes - they need your condition and dose
Only if it is a prescription medicine
Only if they ask you in front of the crew
A
You only need to say that it may affect your ability to work safely. What you tell your supervisor is kept confidential.
OHS-31
You have a valid prescription for medicinal cannabis containing THC. Can you lawfully drive a work vehicle on the road with THC in your system?
Yes - the prescription is a defence
Yes - as long as you feel fine
Yes - it became legal in March 2025
No - any THC at all is an offence
D
Since 1 March 2025 a magistrate can decide not to cancel your licence, but driving with any THC is still an offence. Talk to your supervisor privately about safe duties.
OHS-31
Under Victorian law, what is the position for someone taking a CBD-only medicine (no THC)?
They can never drive a vehicle
They can drive if not impaired
They must show police their script
They can only drive in daylight
B
CBD-only medicines do not contain THC. Patients can lawfully drive as long as they are not impaired - check with your doctor or pharmacist what your product contains.
OHS-31
According to WorkSafe Victoria, being awake for 17 hours affects your performance about as much as what?
A 0.05 blood alcohol level
A 0.02 blood alcohol level
A 0.15 blood alcohol level
It has no measurable effect
A
Seventeen hours awake is about the same as 0.05 BAC, and 20 hours about the same as 0.1. Fatigue is a real impairment.
OHS-31
At 6am a crew member is unsteady, slurring and confused. What should the supervisor do first?
Send them out on a quiet job away from others
Tell them off in front of the crew as a warning
Stop their work and check for a medical cause
Send them home in their own car to sleep it off
C
Low blood sugar, a head injury, heat illness or a stroke can look like intoxication. Stop the work, rule out a medical cause (call 000 if serious), then talk privately.
OHS-31
A supervisor stands a crew member down because they are clearly not fit for work. They want to drive themselves home. What should happen?
Let them go - it is their own car after all
Let them if they promise to go slowly
Hold them in the lunchroom until knock-off
Arrange a safe way home - no driving
D
Someone who is not fit for work must never drive home impaired. Help arrange a safe way home, and call the police if they insist on driving - do not physically restrain anyone.
OHS-31
You keep drifting off your lines on the fairway mower and you feel your head nodding. What do you do?
Stop safely, switch off, tell your supervisor
Turn your music up loud and push on through
Speed up so you get the fairway finished sooner
Have an energy drink and keep on mowing
A
Drowsiness on a machine is a serious risk. Stop safely and tell your supervisor - reporting fatigue is a safety report, not a weakness.
OHS-31
Does the Club run alcohol or drug testing?
Yes - random breath tests every morning
Yes - but only after an incident occurs
No - supervisors judge fitness for work
Only for staff on the spray team
C
Victoria's OHS laws neither require nor prohibit testing. The Club does not test; supervisors are the check, so speak up early if you are not fit.
OHS-35
Which of these is personal information?
Only a name together with a home address
Only details stamped or marked confidential
Anything that could identify a person
Only details stored on a Club computer
C
Personal information is anything that could identify a person - including photos. Health details like medical certificates are sensitive information and need extra care.
OHS-35
A member rings the shed asking for a greenkeeper's mobile number. What do you do?
Take a message and pass it on to them
Give it out, since the member knows them
Text the number to the member later on
Give it out if the member says it is urgent
A
Share personal details only with people who need them for work. Taking a message protects your colleague and still helps the member.
OHS-35
You email a list of member contact details to the wrong person by mistake. What should you do?
Say nothing and hope they ignore it
Delete it from your sent items folder
Wait a week and see if anyone complains
Tell management about it straight away
D
Report breaches immediately so they can be assessed, and tell management anything you did to contain it. Honest mistakes reported quickly are treated as mistakes.
OHS-35
A member rolls a cart into a bunker. A crew member starts filming to post it. What should happen?
Film it, then blur the member's face later
Check they are OK, then report - no filming
Film it, but only share it in the crew chat
Film it as evidence, then post it online
B
Never film injuries or incidents to share. Check on the person, get help, radio your supervisor and report. Group chats are not private.
OHS-35
You take a great photo of juniors at a clinic. Can you post it on your own Instagram?
Yes - it is a positive photo of the Club
Yes - as long as their names are not tagged
No - juniors never go on personal accounts
Yes - if the clinic coach says it is fine
C
Child Safe Standards require clubs to manage risks to children, including online. Photos of juniors need Club permission and parent consent, and never go on personal accounts.
OHS-35
A golfer abuses you on the course. You want to post a video naming him. What should you do?
Tell your supervisor - don't post it
Post it, but only on a private account
Post it with his cart number but no name
Post it and tag the Club so they see it
A
Abuse is never OK and should be reported, but a public post breaches policy and could expose you to legal action. The Club follows up.
OHS-35
Under Victorian law, where must an employer never use cameras or listening devices to monitor workers?
The car park and the clubhouse entrance
The machinery shed and the workshop
Anywhere outdoors on the golf course
Toilets, washrooms and change rooms
D
The Surveillance Devices Act bans employers from monitoring workers in toilets, washrooms, change rooms and lactation rooms.
OHS-35
A journalist calls you about an incident on the course. What do you do?
Give your side so the story is accurate
Politely pass their details to management
Say it is confidential and hang up on them
Answer only the questions about the course
B
Only people authorised by management speak for the Club. Be polite, say you are not the right person, and refer the call on.
OHS-35
You want to post a sunrise photo taken outside the shed. In the corner you can read the keypad code for the chemical store. What do you do?
Post it - nobody will notice the code
Post it, but only to your close friends
Crop it out and tell your supervisor
Post it, then delete it after a day
C
Codes, keys, alarm panels and security set-ups are confidential. Never post them - and report the exposed code so it can be fixed.
OHS-35
Where should you raise a concern about privacy or social media?
Your supervisor or management
A post in the #ohs Slack channel
A post on your own social media
A message in the crew group chat
A
Privacy and social media concerns go to your supervisor or management. #ohs is for safety hazards and incidents only.
